breakdown.description: The prompt collapses the distributed self-weight into a single end load and calls it exact, even though the axial force from self-weight varies continuously along the bar.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification explicitly repeats and reinforces the incorrect instruction from the incomplete prompt. It instructs to 'Treat this total weight W as a single concentrated load applied at the free (bottom) end of the bar' and to 'Use this concentrated load as the axial force P acting uniformly over the entire length of the bar,' then compute δ = P × L / (A × E). The agent even acknowledges in its preamble that this method gives double the correct answer (ρgL²/E vs ρgL²/(2E)) but proceeds with the flawed approach anyway. The ground truth removes this incorrect instruction entirely and relies solely on the correct integral method δ = ∫₀ᴸ P(x)/(AE) dx with the varying axial force P(x) = ρgA(L−x). The inconsistency was not resolved.
